exposure: parity (nulliparous vs. parous) among women undergoing Cesarean Delivery on Maternal Request (CDMR)
cohort: The study cohort consisted of 336 low-risk nulliparous and parous women (second birth and first cesarean delivery) who elected for Cesarean Delivery on Maternal Request (CDMR).
finding: Nulliparous women undergoing CDMR experienced a higher incidence of short-term maternal complications (delayed breastfeeding, increased pain, PCEA activations, pruritus, mastitis, prolonged hospital stays) and neonatal complications (neonatal jaundice requiring hospitalization) compared to parous women.
